Select models, like the new Olive 18 Pro Silicone case have now dropped again to a new Amazon all-time low at 25% off, and you’ll find loads more with deals below. extraction.body: Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence. Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two. Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. Three more Verge-approved deals: * If you’ve been meaning to pick up Pikmin 4, Walmart is selling a digital copy for $39.88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99. It’s the original Switch version, but you can upgrade to the forthcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Edition when it arrives on November 12th by purchasing a separate $9.99 upgrade pack, which adds improved graphics and a new Dandori Academy mode. That brings your total to just $49.87, saving you about $20 compared to buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright. I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors for just $5.99 with a 90-day warranty. The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon. * Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is on sale for $45.99 ($44 off) at Amazon, which is $5 shy of its best price to date. It’s a handy cordless option for small tasks ranging from tightening screws to assembling desks, with 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling a variety of jobs. The USB-C rechargeable screwdriver also comes with a 220RPM motor and three torque settings, along with a LED light to help illuminate your workspace.

Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon.
Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests.
You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching.
Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence.
Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected.

While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location.
The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two.
Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K.

Three more Verge-approved deals: * If you’ve been meaning to pick up Pikmin 4, Walmart is selling a digital copy for $39.88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99.

It’s the original Switch version, but you can upgrade to the forthcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Edition when it arrives on November 12th by purchasing a separate $9.99 upgrade pack, which adds improved graphics and a new Dandori Academy mode.
That brings your total to just $49.87, saving you about $20 compared to buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright.
I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors for just $5.99 with a 90-day warranty.

The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon. * Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is on sale for $45.99 ($44 off) at Amazon, which is $5 shy of its best price to date.
It’s a handy cordless option for small tasks ranging from tightening screws to assembling desks, with 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling a variety of jobs.
The USB-C rechargeable screwdriver also comes with a 220RPM motor and three torque settings, along with a LED light to help illuminate your workspace.

extraction.body: Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence. Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two. Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. Three more Verge-approved deals: * If you’ve been meaning to pick up Pikmin 4, Walmart is selling a digital copy for $39.88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99. It’s the original Switch version, but you can upgrade to the forthcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Edition when it arrives on November 12th by purchasing a separate $9.99 upgrade pack, which adds improved graphics and a new Dandori Academy mode. That brings your total to just $49.87, saving you about $20 compared to buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright. I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors for just $5.99 with a 90-day warranty. The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon. * Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is on sale for $45.99 ($44 off) at Amazon, which is $5 shy of its best price to date. It’s a handy cordless option for small tasks ranging from tightening screws to assembling desks, with 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling a variety of jobs. The USB-C rechargeable screwdriver also comes with a 220RPM motor and three torque settings, along with a LED light to help illuminate your workspace.

sources.title: Tesla's new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won't land until 2028 - Yahoo Finance
passages: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.
A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla ​says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system."
The original Roadster, released ​in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used ​a Lotus Elise chassis.
It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be.
The company has since been known for its Model Y and ‌Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans.
"The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said.
"Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology.
The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month.
The Roadster can also travel over ‌300 miles (480 km) on a single charge.
That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when ​Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020.

The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.

The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket ‌company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters.
Tesla shares were up 5% in premarket trading on Friday.

"It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X.
"That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X.
"I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI."
Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle.
Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over ‌the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter.
The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown.
It also launched Cybercab — a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car. The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket ‌company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters. Later in the event it used the thrusters ‌to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver. Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing ​their overlap. Tesla shares were up 5% in premarket trading on Friday. The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors. "It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X. "The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing ‌it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the ⁠needle in a major way financially." "Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Viewers and witnesses ⁠gushed over the spectacle of the launch. "That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI." Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed ​a "Performance" ​version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla ​says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system." The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown. "This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors. The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph (370 kph), Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said. "Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound." The Roadster can also travel over ‌300 miles (480 km) on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when ​Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020. The original Roadster, released ​in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used ​a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and ‌Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans. The reveal of ​the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in ​Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab — a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors. Tesla is set to report third-quarter results ​on October 21. Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over ‌the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter. "The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than ​anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro. (Reporting by Abhirup Roy in San Francisco and Mrinmay Dey in ​Mexico City; Additional reporting by Chris Thomas and Chris Kirkham; Editing by Peter Henderson and Tom Hogue)

sources.title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
passages: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style Sean O'Kane
Tesla just revealed its redesigned second-generation Roadster with SpaceX thrusters, a vehicle CEO Elon Musk has called “the best of the last of the human-driven cars.”
Unveiled as a surprise at the end of the Tesla Semi reveal in 2017, the revamped Roadster was supposed to be delivered in just a few years.
Tesla allowed customers to place $50,000 deposits to reserve the car.
Some even paid $250,000 to reserve one of 1,000 “Founders Series” versions.
Engineering VP Lars Moravy said at the event that the Roadster uses 10 thrusters connected to 600 liters of compressed air to lift and spin the car in midair.
The company said “every usable void” in the car is filled with these vessels.
One week later , at the shareholder meeting where he was awarded a $1 trillion pay package, he delayed it to April 1, 2026.
Musk said holding an April Fools’ Day event would give him “some deniability” if Tesla delayed the event again.
Maybe they will even allow a Tesla to fly …”

Musk has positioned the Roadster as a true halo car for Tesla, saying at one point that he’s “not sure it moves the needle massively from a revenue standpoint.” But he has previously said that “safety is not the main goal” with the new Roadster.
Tesla would “aspire not to kill anyone in this car,” he said.
You know when I suggested this to the team, I thought, ‘Am I crazy?’”
Tesla wound up pushing back the reveal again.
It attempted to hold the event on October 1, but severe weather forced yet another delay.

“This will be the actual car that’s on the roads,” Musk said of the car, which Tesla showed accelerating 0 to 60 miles per hour in one second. “It literally is just going to puff itself up, and uh, and be able to do this, these maneuvers whenever you’d like.”
Musk said Tesla will finally build the long-delayed vehicle in 2028, but didn’t name a price.
The third is “Rocket,” which is “air ready” and seats one, and has 10 cold-gas thrusters positioned around the car.
The Rocket trim is billed as “invite only.”
In another post, Tesla said the design was inspired by the SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft and the F-35 fighter jet.

sources.title: Tesla Teases an October 1 Roadster Reveal Featuring a Hovering Car Powered by SpaceX Thrusters - Hypebeast
passages: This deafening exhibition serves as a high-visibility demonstration of engineering synergy between Elon Musk ’s two largest companies.
Shared hardware between Tesla and SpaceX illustrates the operational overlap Musk wishes to highlight.
Investors are the target of this theatrical stunt as the chief executive seeks Wall Street support for a potential merger of the two entities.
The event functions as a visceral pitch for a unified technological future rather than a traditional product launch.
The machine hitting the pad on October 1 differs significantly from the consumer sports car originally promised.
This hovering car is not street legal and will likely cost hundreds of thousands of dollars.
Plans at the automaker involve selling this extreme iteration exclusively to superfans through a dedicated track program.
Such a strategy mimics the hyper-exclusive client playbook used by Ferrari.
Recent changes follow nearly a decade of missed targets for the Tesla Roadster.
The 2017 prototype promised a $200,000 base price, a 620-mile range and a top speed exceeding 250 mph.
Reservation holders paid up to $250,000 to secure a Founders Series allocation for a 2020 production target that never arrived.
Manufacturing delays occurred at least eight times over the following years.
Musk conceded at a November shareholder meeting that production will not begin until 2027 or 2028.
Such setbacks led prominent early adopters like Marques Brownlee and Sam Altman to cancel their six-figure reservations.
Stamped with a “10.01” date and the caption “Go for launch,” the artwork depicts a red car bathed in stark vertical lighting that mirrors a rocket launch pad.
A ticking clock is now live on the automaker’s official webpage.
Location and broadcast details remain unconfirmed for the spectacle.
The planned demonstration revolves around SpaceX-developed cold gas thrusters integrated into the vehicle to allow it to hover.

Musk presented the car at SpaceX's test site in McGregor, Texas, where it climbed a curved wall, hung nearly upside down on suction fans and flipped over a row of Tesla models. A live run clocked 0.81 seconds from zero to 60 mph, and Musk said the production car should beat that time. No human drove the car during the stunts, a choice Musk said was meant to avoid killing anyone. After the show, Tesla listed three versions, starting with a two-seat Performance model that reaches 60 mph in under 1.6 seconds and a limited-run Thrust that adds rear cold-gas thrusters to get under 0.9 seconds. The single-seat Rocket, offered by invitation only, can lift off the ground and top 230 mph, but Tesla says it is not approved for public roads. Ten compressed-air nozzles fed by a 600-liter tank, which the car can refill on its own, provide the thrust, and every version claims more than 300 miles of range. Tesla has not released battery or motor details. It gave no price either, but U.S. buyers must put down $50,000 to reserve a Performance car and $250,000 for a Thrust, the same sums it collected in 2017. Thursday's show capped nearly nine years of missed deadlines.

Later in the event it used the thrusters ‌to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver. Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing ​their overlap. Tesla shares were up 5% in premarket trading on Friday. The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors. "The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing ‌it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the ⁠needle in a major way financially." "Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Viewers and witnesses ⁠gushed over the spectacle of the launch. "That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI." Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed ​a "Performance" ​version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla ​says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system." The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown. "This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors. The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph (370 kph), Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said. "Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound." The Roadster can also travel over ‌300 miles (480 km) on a single charge. The reveal of ​the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in ​Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. extraction.body: Tesla just revealed its redesigned second-generation Roadster with SpaceX thrusters, a vehicle CEO Elon Musk has called “the best of the last of the human-driven cars.” Musk showed off the car at an event outside Waco, Texas, with a demonstration that saw the car use a mixture of high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin around, and ease itself to a landing on the pavement below. The car also used the thrusters to lift itself over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 while in motion. “This will be the actual car that’s on the roads,” Musk said of the car, which Tesla showed accelerating 0 to 60 miles per hour in one second. “It literally is just going to puff itself up, and uh, and be able to do this, these maneuvers whenever you’d like.” Musk said Tesla will finally build the long-delayed vehicle in 2028, but didn’t name a price. Tesla will offer it in three trims. The first is “Performance,” which Tesla describes as “road ready.” It seats two, has active aerodynamics, and features a “multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off the track.” The second trim is “Thrust,” which is “race ready” and seats two, and has rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable sub-one-second 0-to-60 mph acceleration. The third is “Rocket,” which is “air ready” and seats one, and has 10 cold-gas thrusters positioned around the car. All three trims will have 300 miles of range and be capable of speeds exceeding 230 miles per hour. Tesla’s website showed Thursday the company is taking reservations for the car, charging $50,000 just to reserve the Performance, and $250,000 for Thrust. The Rocket trim is billed as “invite only.” Engineering VP Lars Moravy said at the event that the Roadster uses 10 thrusters connected to 600 liters of compressed air to lift and spin the car in midair. The air tank can be recharged, he said. “Every usable void in the car is packed with Carbon Fiber Overwrapped Pressure Vessels (COPVs),” Tesla wrote in a post on X, referring to the type of pressure vessel that has been at the root of multiple SpaceX rocket explosions. The company said “every usable void” in the car is filled with these vessels. Musk also said at the event that Tesla may try to jump the Snake River Canyon — the site of Evel Knievel’s famous attempt to cross the gorge in a steam-powered rocket. Musk has positioned the Roadster as a true halo car for Tesla, saying at one point that he’s “not sure it moves the needle massively from a revenue standpoint.” But he has previously said that “safety is not the main goal” with the new Roadster. “If you buy a Ferrari, safety is not the number one goal. I say, if safety is your number one goal, do not buy the Roadster,” he said on a podcast earlier this year . Tesla would “aspire not to kill anyone in this car,” he said. “This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX Engineers working closely together to make something you haven’t seen in any movie, better than any James Bond car,” Musk said at the event. “I’ve never seen anything like this. You know when I suggested this to the team, I thought, ‘Am I crazy?’” Musk had previously claimed that the car “will be very different from what was shown previously” and promised the demo would be the “most exciting, whether it works or not, demo ever of any product.” The design changes were notable. The car, shown in stark white, now has a more angular design reminiscent of a Lamborghini or the famous Lotus Esprit used by the James Bond character in “The Spy Who Loved Me” — a car Musk owns , which was on display at the event. The third is “Rocket,” which is “air ready” and seats one, and has 10 cold-gas thrusters positioned around the car.
All three trims will have 300 miles of range and be capable of speeds exceeding 230 miles per hour.
Tesla’s website showed Thursday the company is taking reservations for the car, charging $50,000 just to reserve the Performance, and $250,000 for Thrust. The Rocket trim is billed as “invite only.”

sources.title: Tesla Teases an October 1 Roadster Reveal Featuring a Hovering Car Powered by SpaceX Thrusters - Hypebeast
passages: This deafening exhibition serves as a high-visibility demonstration of engineering synergy between Elon Musk ’s two largest companies.
Shared hardware between Tesla and SpaceX illustrates the operational overlap Musk wishes to highlight.
Investors are the target of this theatrical stunt as the chief executive seeks Wall Street support for a potential merger of the two entities.
The event functions as a visceral pitch for a unified technological future rather than a traditional product launch.
The machine hitting the pad on October 1 differs significantly from the consumer sports car originally promised.
This hovering car is not street legal and will likely cost hundreds of thousands of dollars.
Plans at the automaker involve selling this extreme iteration exclusively to superfans through a dedicated track program.
Such a strategy mimics the hyper-exclusive client playbook used by Ferrari.
Recent changes follow nearly a decade of missed targets for the Tesla Roadster.
The 2017 prototype promised a $200,000 base price, a 620-mile range and a top speed exceeding 250 mph.
Reservation holders paid up to $250,000 to secure a Founders Series allocation for a 2020 production target that never arrived.
Manufacturing delays occurred at least eight times over the following years.
Musk conceded at a November shareholder meeting that production will not begin until 2027 or 2028.
Such setbacks led prominent early adopters like Marques Brownlee and Sam Altman to cancel their six-figure reservations.
Stamped with a “10.01” date and the caption “Go for launch,” the artwork depicts a red car bathed in stark vertical lighting that mirrors a rocket launch pad.
A ticking clock is now live on the automaker’s official webpage.
Location and broadcast details remain unconfirmed for the spectacle.
The planned demonstration revolves around SpaceX-developed cold gas thrusters integrated into the vehicle to allow it to hover.
Tesla Sets Roadster Reveal Date, RSVP Deadline Looms

passages: Elon Musk showed off Tesla 's long-delayed Roadster on Thursday, flying it over parked cars on SpaceX thrusters and hitting 60 mph in 0.81 seconds, with production set for 2028.

Tesla shares rose nearly 3% in overnight trading, but Gene Munster , managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management , called the reveal an "engineering flex" with little commercial value beyond showing up traditional carmakers.
He also read the event as a sign that Musk is eager to bring Tesla and SpaceX together, calling the car a "mashup of the two tech teams."
Tesla first showed the second-generation Roadster in November 2017, promising a 1.9-second sprint to 60 mph, a 620-mile range, a $200,000 base price and deliveries in 2020.
Alexey Bondarev is Head of Content at Yellow.com.

Musk, who said the Roadster would eventually be Tesla's only manually driven car, conceded it is "not necessarily a safety-optimized car." Asked by a spectator whether it was street legal, he replied: "It depends on your street."
Musk presented the car at SpaceX's test site in McGregor, Texas, where it climbed a curved wall, hung nearly upside down on suction fans and flipped over a row of Tesla models.

Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app. But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ). That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView . Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home . "Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," Counterpoint Research research director Mohit Agrawal said in a note following Apple's Welcome Home event on Tuesday. "Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added. The HomeView takes a lot of its software design cues from the Apple Watch , complete with a series of built-in clock faces. There's a hub screen that lets you control your smart home devices, such as lights, locks, and thermostats, as well as an iPhone-like home screen where you can open apps like FaceTime or Messages. Users can also view multiple smart camera feeds, use the HomeView's built-in camera as a vanity mirror before they head out the door, and look up things like recipes from their iPhones and then project them on the screen. Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView. Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions. The company designed the HomeView to recognize six faces via its facial recognition camera. If you want to access your personal messages, calendar, and so on, you'll need your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub so it can authenticate you. Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup. The new hardware provides users with a long-awaited Apple-built solution for controlling smart home devices. To date, customers have had to wrangle a collection of do-it-yourself options, such as using iPads as wall-mounted command centers. HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories . The company has also partnered with LG and Schneider Electr ic to produce new smart door locks, thermostats, and indoor and outdoor cameras. But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather. I've been using Siri AI on my iPhone for the past several weeks, and it's proven to be quite helpful when it comes to asking questions related to texts and emails, such as requesting the name of a restaurant my friend suggested I check out. But I haven't been able to try the AI assistant with HomeView just yet. Whether it works as advertised will be integral to the overall experience. "Generative AI has raised expectations for conversational ease and genuinely useful assistance, and Siri has consistently lagged," Forrester vice president and principal analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee said in a press statement. "The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained. If Apple's strategy to take smart home share from Amazon and Google succeeds, it could provide a boost to the company's bottom line while helping to ensure increased lock-in among its customers. Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories. That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025. That's better than its Mac and iPad businesses, but nowhere near its Services division, which brought in $109.15 billion, or its iPhone arm, which generated $209.59 billion in the same period. sources.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
passages: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform.
Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition.

Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

“But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices.
Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t?
Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi.

"“The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app.”" - Kaiann Drance, Apple According to Apple, setup is as simple as tapping your iPhone to the device, like pairing AirPods, with no extra account or app needed and no scanning required.
This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home.
The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates.
They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display.
Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView.
It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers.

extraction.body: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform. The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell, all codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display. Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition. Amazon’s and Google’s ecosystems support more products, and both have popular in-house brands: Ring and Nest. Apple had nothing of its own to point customers to as an Apple experience — and now it does. And does Apple actually add anything new here, or is this mostly packaging? The second was AI, which brought a more conversational Siri voice assistant. Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” Drance says. “That’s been a really critical piece of bringing this all together.” The bigger play here is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home for Apple’s users. Buy one for playing music, guided cooking recipes, and checking your calendar, and you might soon want a camera or smart lock to go with it. Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do. The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates. Privacy and security concerns and complexity also rank high, along with cost. While Apple isn’t addressing the cost concern here — the products start at $200 — the other elements are part of its pitch: one-tap setup, your data stays yours, one app to run it all. Apple’s stamp of approval also carries a lot of weight. The Home Collection is more like the chef’s choice, a short list of dishes Apple promises will pair well. “There is a lot of choice with Matter, and there’s a lot of great products out there,” she says. “But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices. Drance says setup and ease of use were a big focus. “The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app,” she says. “We just wanted that simplicity to be at its core, and of course, the privacy that we’ve developed together with our partners.” She says everything integrates through Apple Home; you don’t need to create an LG or Schneider account, and all data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can access it. Drance was clear that the Apple Home Collection isn’t replacing the buffet — the hardware ecosystem that has grown up around Apple Home. “We still have this incredible ecosystem with Matter, and with Works with Apple Home, that is going to remain,” she says. “We know that homes are not a one-size-fits-all solution, so our customers will continue to have that choice, and we remain committed to building that ecosystem as well.” The hardware mostly backs that up. The exception is the cameras, which use Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video, not Matter. I was surprised Apple didn’t announce Matter camera support. But the Thread radios suggest the hardware might be Matter-ready, and Apple may be waiting for the Matter camera standard to support encrypted uploads, something HKSV already does. Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t? “What we’ve done with Apple Home Collection is we’ve added another layer on top of that, that deeper integration,” says Drance. There aren’t features exclusive to the Home Collection; it’s more that Apple is saying all the features will be here. It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers. Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi. This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home.

The tech giant has been mousy when it comes to smart home tech, but rumors are swirling about an Apple smart home display, security cameras and other home devices ahead of Tuesday's event. Apple’s smart home line is set to arrive in the near future. Here’s what I’m excited about. It’s a matter of when, not if. Apple’s take on the smart home is coming, with multiple reports saying the tech giant is ready to release its own line of smart devices and home security products . While it’s a little early, Apple’s big “awe dropping” event on Sept. 9 could showcase the first elements of its big home expansion. We already expect to see the new iPhone 17 , a new Apple Watch and an AirPod announcement . Here’s what could happen if there’s a surprise home tech release, too, from table robots to home security cameras. Don’t miss any of our unbiased tech content and lab-based reviews. The rumor is Apple’s tabletop robot , a smart 7-inch screen mounted to a swiveling arm that can move to face various people sitting around in a living room, kitchen, office or other space. It sounds a bit like Amazon’s swiveling Echo Show 10 (currently discontinued as Amazon appears to be working on an updated model), albeit with an Apple focus on FaceTime for video chats. The “robot” part is largely due to Bubbles, a code name for an updated version of Siri. Apple has been working on several different versions of Siri with more conversational AI features. For the tabletop display, Siri would gain the ability to hold conversations with multiple people at once, and a first-ever animated icon to give Siri a “face” to use in conversations. These new versions of Siri seem to be central to Apple’s smart home plans, but I’m not sure if they’ll see the light of day now that Apple is working on empowering Siri with Google Gemini AI . The robot is ambitious and unlikely to appear at Apple’s fall event. Swiveling smart displays are a tough sell, not to mention mechanical arms, which make displays far more fragile, difficult to use and potentially intrusive. Apple’s smart display could be an expect evolution of its HomePod line. If Apple wants to make a big smart home splash while staying relatively safe and showing off its display prowess (two things Apple loves to do), the fall event may include a smart display . The 7-inch smart display would include many features of the robot, including the bubblier version of Siri, but would stay in one place like most smart displays. Rumors say Apple is focusing on Apple Watch-like widgets and clock faces for such a display, in a new UI labeled Charismatic. Such a screen could serve as a smart alarm clock, home hub or music device, with Siri serving a central role as controller and operator of the display’s various functions. Apple is rumored to release its own security camera after supporting brands like Logitech in the past. With competitors like Amazon’s Ring and Google Nest well-known for their security cameras , it’s no surprise that Apple is considering an entry, as well. According to Bloomberg’s sources , Apple has been experimenting with a variety of camera designs to create a model (code J450, apparently, no snazzy code names here) that can work with the rest of Apple’s smart home. Rumored specs sound familiar to many security cams I’ve tested, including wireless and battery-powered capabilities, plus facial recognition and motion detection. But there’s no firm word on resolution or outdoor capabilities yet. Apple also wants its camera to connect closely with other smart home devices, such as turning lights on and off using its presence-sensing features. An Apple doorbell could compete with models from Nest, ring and more. I’ve heard very little about the possibility of an Apple doorbell, but it fits well with the rest of these rumors. So far, reports only mention that Apple has tested a video doorbell concept . However, it’s one of the easiest entry points into the smart home for buyers and sellers alike, and brands like Nest split their lines into security cams and video doorbells, as well. So even if Apple isn’t quite ready to launch a doorbell yet, I’d bet it happens around the same time as its security camera or soon afterward. I’ll keep you updated on the latest Apple home news, if and when any big announcements hit. For now, take a look at Apple’s competition with my guides to the best smart speakers , best home security cameras and the best security systems . © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All of this is part of the Cupertino giant’s push into creating a complete home devices category.

Apple is entering a smart display category where Amazon and Google have had products for years, and analysts have previously pointed out that the harder problem was never the hardware — it’s getting people to actually wire up a smart home in the first place.

There’s also an irony sitting underneath the entire Siri AI push: Apple has previously confirmed it enlisted Google’s help this year to get Siri’s underlying capabilities up to scratch, meaning the assistant central to Apple’s pitch for its own hardware ecosystem has a rival’s fingerprints on it.

Ternus inherits a company investors have been watching more closely for hardware growth as its services business faces regulatory pressure, and a new product category gives him something fresh to point to.

When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, it can pull in personal context from Calendar, Messages and other apps to give more useful answers, and conversations started on HomeView sync via iCloud so they can continue on an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch or Vision Pro.

It gets an A19 chip that Apple says delivers up to 50% faster CPU performance and twice the graphics performance of its predecessor, three built-in far-field microphones so people can talk to Siri without touching the remote, and an updated Siri Remote with Find My support and Precision Finding.

extraction.body: Apple's first smart home hub, HomeView, arrives alongside a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini — though Siri AI isn't ready on all of them yet. Apple made its long-rumored move into the smart home hub category official on Tuesday , unveiling HomeView alongside refreshed versions of the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini at its “Welcome Home” event in New York. The launch is also a personal milestone of sorts: it’s the first major hardware event for John Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief executive on September 1 after 25 years at the company, most recently as the executive running hardware engineering. Ternus inherits a company investors have been watching more closely for hardware growth as its services business faces regulatory pressure, and a new product category gives him something fresh to point to. HomeView is a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, sold in a tabletop version with a domed aluminium speaker base and stainless steel tilting hinge, and a separate wall-mounted version, both priced at $299 in the US. The tabletop model comes in silver, starlight, rose pink and space gray, while the wall-mounted version ships in space gray and silver. It runs on an A18 chip and uses a front-facing camera to recognize up to six different household members by face, switching automatically between a shared household screen and a personalized one. Pre-orders opened Tuesday, with the device arriving November 13. The headline feature is Siri AI, an entirely new, more conversational version of Siri built on Apple’s next-generation Apple Intelligence. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, it can pull in personal context from Calendar, Messages and other apps to give more useful answers, and conversations started on HomeView sync via iCloud so they can continue on an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch or Vision Pro. Apple’s Greg Joswiak, the company’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing, framed the pitch simply: HomeView is “designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user.” Beyond the assistant, HomeView functions as a household command center — FaceTime calls with Center Stage, Intercom, Apple Music with animated lyrics, Apple TV, Apple News and Apple Podcasts, plus control over accessories and scenes from Apple’s new Home Collection accessory line, which adds outdoor cameras, temperature sensors and access management into the same screen. The new Apple TV 4K, its first update in four years, is a more substantial overhaul than usual. It gets an A19 chip that Apple says delivers up to 50% faster CPU performance and twice the graphics performance of its predecessor, three built-in far-field microphones so people can talk to Siri without touching the remote, and an updated Siri Remote with Find My support and Precision Finding. Apple is also leaning on it as a smart home hub in its own right, using Apple Intelligence to generate camera activity descriptions and summarize notifications inside the Home app. It’s priced at $299, in a single 128GB configuration, and also ships November 13. Bob Borchers, Apple’s vice president of worldwide product marketing, called it the company’s “most immersive home theater experience yet.” The HomePod mini refresh is where the Siri AI story gets more complicated. The new $149 speaker, up $50 from the original 2020 model, gets an S10 chip for better sound and the ability to recognize sounds like a smoke alarm and alert a user’s phone, a feature Alexa devices have had for years. But Apple has confirmed that Siri AI itself won’t be available on the new HomePod mini at launch; it’s coming later through a software update, with no date given. That’s a notable gap in a launch built almost entirely around the promise of a smarter Siri everywhere in the home, and it lands on a different schedule than the rest of the lineup: the new HomePod mini ships October 30, two weeks before HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K. All of this is part of the Cupertino giant’s push into creating a complete home devices category. Apple is entering a smart display category where Amazon and Google have had products for years, and analysts have previously pointed out that the harder problem was never the hardware — it’s getting people to actually wire up a smart home in the first place. There’s also an irony sitting underneath the entire Siri AI push: Apple has previously confirmed it enlisted Google’s help this year to get Siri’s underlying capabilities up to scratch, meaning the assistant central to Apple’s pitch for its own hardware ecosystem has a rival’s fingerprints on it. Whether that matters to the people actually buying a $299 screen for their kitchen counter is a different question than whether Apple can build one. Tuesday’s event answered the second question. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app.
But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories.
That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025.
That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView .

Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home .
Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView.
Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup.
"The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained.
HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories .
"Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added.
But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather.
For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform.
Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition.

Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

“But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices.
Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t?
Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi.

"“The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app.”" - Kaiann Drance, Apple According to Apple, setup is as simple as tapping your iPhone to the device, like pairing AirPods, with no extra account or app needed and no scanning required.
This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home.
The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates.
They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display.

Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app. But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ). That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView . Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home . "Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," Counterpoint Research research director Mohit Agrawal said in a note following Apple's Welcome Home event on Tuesday. "Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added. The HomeView takes a lot of its software design cues from the Apple Watch , complete with a series of built-in clock faces. There's a hub screen that lets you control your smart home devices, such as lights, locks, and thermostats, as well as an iPhone-like home screen where you can open apps like FaceTime or Messages. Users can also view multiple smart camera feeds, use the HomeView's built-in camera as a vanity mirror before they head out the door, and look up things like recipes from their iPhones and then project them on the screen. Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView. Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions. The company designed the HomeView to recognize six faces via its facial recognition camera. If you want to access your personal messages, calendar, and so on, you'll need your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub so it can authenticate you. Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup. The new hardware provides users with a long-awaited Apple-built solution for controlling smart home devices. To date, customers have had to wrangle a collection of do-it-yourself options, such as using iPads as wall-mounted command centers. HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories . The company has also partnered with LG and Schneider Electr ic to produce new smart door locks, thermostats, and indoor and outdoor cameras. But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather. I've been using Siri AI on my iPhone for the past several weeks, and it's proven to be quite helpful when it comes to asking questions related to texts and emails, such as requesting the name of a restaurant my friend suggested I check out. But I haven't been able to try the AI assistant with HomeView just yet. Whether it works as advertised will be integral to the overall experience. "Generative AI has raised expectations for conversational ease and genuinely useful assistance, and Siri has consistently lagged," Forrester vice president and principal analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee said in a press statement. Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app. But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).

That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView . Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home .

"Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," Counterpoint Research research director Mohit Agrawal said in a note following Apple's Welcome Home event on Tuesday.
"Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added.

The HomeView takes a lot of its software design cues from the Apple Watch , complete with a series of built-in clock faces. There's a hub screen that lets you control your smart home devices, such as lights, locks, and thermostats, as well as an iPhone-like home screen where you can open apps like FaceTime or Messages.

Users can also view multiple smart camera feeds, use the HomeView's built-in camera as a vanity mirror before they head out the door, and look up things like recipes from their iPhones and then project them on the screen.

Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView. Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions.

The company designed the HomeView to recognize six faces via its facial recognition camera. If you want to access your personal messages, calendar, and so on, you'll need your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub so it can authenticate you.
Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup.

The new hardware provides users with a long-awaited Apple-built solution for controlling smart home devices. To date, customers have had to wrangle a collection of do-it-yourself options, such as using iPads as wall-mounted command centers.
HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories .
The company has also partnered with LG and Schneider Electr ic to produce new smart door locks, thermostats, and indoor and outdoor cameras.
But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather.

I've been using Siri AI on my iPhone for the past several weeks, and it's proven to be quite helpful when it comes to asking questions related to texts and emails, such as requesting the name of a restaurant my friend suggested I check out.
But I haven't been able to try the AI assistant with HomeView just yet. Whether it works as advertised will be integral to the overall experience.

"Generative AI has raised expectations for conversational ease and genuinely useful assistance, and Siri has consistently lagged," Forrester vice president and principal analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee said in a press statement.
"The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained.
If Apple's strategy to take smart home share from Amazon and Google succeeds, it could provide a boost to the company's bottom line while helping to ensure increased lock-in among its customers.

Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories. That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025.
That's better than its Mac and iPad businesses, but nowhere near its Services division, which brought in $109.15 billion, or its iPhone arm, which generated $209.59 billion in the same period.

Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition.

Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi.

This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home.

extraction.body: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform. The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell, all codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display. Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still feels underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition. Amazon’s and Google’s ecosystems support more products, and both have popular in-house brands: Ring and Nest. Apple had nothing of its own to point customers to as an Apple experience — and now it does. And does Apple actually add anything new here, or is this mostly packaging? The second was AI, which brought a more conversational Siri voice assistant. Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” Drance says. “That’s been a really critical piece of bringing this all together.” The bigger play here is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home for Apple’s users. Buy one for playing music, guided cooking recipes, and checking your calendar, and you might soon want a camera or smart lock to go with it. Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do. The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates. Privacy and security concerns and complexity also rank high, along with cost. While Apple isn’t addressing the cost concern here — the products start at $200 — the other elements are part of its pitch: one-tap setup, your data stays yours, one app to run it all. Apple’s stamp of approval also carries a lot of weight. The Home Collection is more like the chef’s choice, a short list of dishes Apple promises will pair well. “There is a lot of choice with Matter, and there’s a lot of great products out there,” she says. “But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices. Drance says setup and ease of use were a big focus. “The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app,” she says. “We just wanted that simplicity to be at its core, and of course, the privacy that we’ve developed together with our partners.” She says everything integrates through Apple Home; you don’t need to create an LG or Schneider account, and all data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can access it. Drance was clear that the Apple Home Collection isn’t replacing the buffet — the hardware ecosystem that has grown up around Apple Home. “We still have this incredible ecosystem with Matter, and with Works with Apple Home, that is going to remain,” she says. “We know that homes are not a one-size-fits-all solution, so our customers will continue to have that choice, and we remain committed to building that ecosystem as well.” The hardware mostly backs that up. The exception is the cameras, which use Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video, not Matter. I was surprised Apple didn’t announce Matter camera support. But the Thread radios suggest the hardware might be Matter-ready, and Apple may be waiting for the Matter camera standard to support encrypted uploads, something HKSV already does. Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t? “What we’ve done with Apple Home Collection is we’ve added another layer on top of that, that deeper integration,” says Drance. There aren’t features exclusive to the Home Collection; it’s more that Apple is saying all the features will be here. It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers. Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi. This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home.

Apple’s smart home line is set to arrive in the near future. Here’s what I’m excited about. It’s a matter of when, not if. Apple’s take on the smart home is coming, with multiple reports saying the tech giant is ready to release its own line of smart devices and home security products . While it’s a little early, Apple’s big “awe dropping” event on Sept. 9 could showcase the first elements of its big home expansion. We already expect to see the new iPhone 17 , a new Apple Watch and an AirPod announcement . Add CNET as a preferred Google source. How do you create something completely new for the smart home space? The rumor is Apple’s tabletop robot , a smart 7-inch screen mounted to a swiveling arm that can move to face various people sitting around in a living room, kitchen, office or other space. It sounds a bit like Amazon’s swiveling Echo Show 10 (currently discontinued as Amazon appears to be working on an updated model), albeit with an Apple focus on FaceTime for video chats. The “robot” part is largely due to Bubbles, a code name for an updated version of Siri. Apple has been working on several different versions of Siri with more conversational AI features. For the tabletop display, Siri would gain the ability to hold conversations with multiple people at once, and a first-ever animated icon to give Siri a “face” to use in conversations. These new versions of Siri seem to be central to Apple’s smart home plans, but I’m not sure if they’ll see the light of day now that Apple is working on empowering Siri with Google Gemini AI . The robot is ambitious and unlikely to appear at Apple’s fall event. Swiveling smart displays are a tough sell, not to mention mechanical arms, which make displays far more fragile, difficult to use and potentially intrusive. Apple’s smart display could be an expect evolution of its HomePod line. If Apple wants to make a big smart home splash while staying relatively safe and showing off its display prowess (two things Apple loves to do), the fall event may include a smart display . The 7-inch smart display would include many features of the robot, including the bubblier version of Siri, but would stay in one place like most smart displays. Rumors say Apple is focusing on Apple Watch-like widgets and clock faces for such a display, in a new UI labeled Charismatic. Such a screen could serve as a smart alarm clock, home hub or music device, with Siri serving a central role as controller and operator of the display’s various functions. Apple is rumored to release its own security camera after supporting brands like Logitech in the past. With competitors like Amazon’s Ring and Google Nest well-known for their security cameras , it’s no surprise that Apple is considering an entry, as well. According to Bloomberg’s sources , Apple has been experimenting with a variety of camera designs to create a model (code J450, apparently, no snazzy code names here) that can work with the rest of Apple’s smart home. Rumored specs sound familiar to many security cams I’ve tested, including wireless and battery-powered capabilities, plus facial recognition and motion detection. But there’s no firm word on resolution or outdoor capabilities yet. Apple also wants its camera to connect closely with other smart home devices, such as turning lights on and off using its presence-sensing features. An Apple doorbell could compete with models from Nest, ring and more. I’ve heard very little about the possibility of an Apple doorbell, but it fits well with the rest of these rumors. So far, reports only mention that Apple has tested a video doorbell concept . However, it’s one of the easiest entry points into the smart home for buyers and sellers alike, and brands like Nest split their lines into security cams and video doorbells, as well. So even if Apple isn’t quite ready to launch a doorbell yet, I’d bet it happens around the same time as its security camera or soon afterward. I’ll keep you updated on the latest Apple home news, if and when any big announcements hit. For now, take a look at Apple’s competition with my guides to the best smart speakers , best home security cameras and the best security systems . © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. An Apple doorbell could compete with models from Nest, ring and more.
